_comment: What each image in src/assets/ actually IS. Authored, never measured — this is
the one input to a check that a program cannot derive.
WHY IT EXISTS. The repo publishes a rule — 'Never fake a product UI out of
rectangles. Use a real screenshot or nothing' — and nothing in `verify` can
enforce it, because every other check here reads text or tokens and this is a
claim baked into a picture. That left exactly one hazard with no mechanism:
artwork provenance was checked by a person opening the file, or it was not
checked. It went unchecked long enough for four reconstructions to ship, and
for a note claiming the Hotels.com captures carried invented figures to sit in
the record for days before anyone opened them and found it false.
WHAT IT CAN AND CANNOT DO. It cannot verify a claim. A person still has to
open the file and be honest about what they see. What it removes is the option
of never being asked: an unclassified image fails the build, so the claim gets
made once, in writing, at the moment the asset lands rather than months later
when someone is trying to remember. Same move as `Metrics` requiring `source`
and `Explorations` requiring `why` — the type system cannot check that a number
is true either, only that somebody said where it came from.
RECONSTRUCTIONS ARE REPORTED ON EVERY RUN, NOT SILENCED. They are accepted, not
hidden: a decision taken once tends to be forgotten, and the whole risk of a
reconstruction is that it stops looking like one. Printing them keeps an
accepted cost visible instead of letting it decay into an assumption.
kind:
capture        A real screenshot of software that actually shipped.
reconstruction Rebuilt to look like a capture of a real interface. THE RISKY
ONE — a reader who knows the tool spots what is wrong, on a
site whose whole argument is that its claims are checkable.
diagram        An explanatory chart. Presents itself as drawn and imitates no
product UI, so it makes no claim to be a capture.
illustration   Abstract or decorative artwork. Depicts nothing and asserts
nothing.
note: what a person saw when they opened it. Required, and 'ok' is not a note.

egds-token-tiers-light.png.note: Generated flat 2D chart of the three token tiers, wired 2026-08-18. Imitates no product UI. The swatches are illustrative and carry NO hex values — an earlier pass had a legend of hex codes and it was cut precisely because those values were of unverified provenance. SUPERSEDED 2026-08-19 by src/components/TokenTiers.tsx, which draws the same picture in elements and is therefore right in both themes; the dark counterpart this file needed was never exported and is no longer wanted. Retained rather than deleted because it is the source the component's palette was sampled from, pixel by pixel, and deleting it would leave that measurement with nothing behind it. Rendered on no page.
